propositions: Test-scale wall-clock windows in review-bot bootstrap, lock-retry, shutdown, and autodeploy coverage consume multi-second costs that can be shortened without changing production timeout and backoff contracts.
Production timeout, retry, drain, health, and backoff defaults must remain unchanged to preserve contractual guarantees.
Real subprocess, lock, process-group, and health boundary behavior must be preserved in test execution even after window shortening.
Window optimization requires injecting or scaling only test-owned clocks while retaining real boundary execution and teardown polling.
Focused test median improved from 56.22s to 29.31s (47.9% reduction), exceeding the 20s aggregate and 50% per-family savings targets.
Each shortened test case retained attempt counts, logical schedules, terminal states, cleanup assertions, and exact-defect mutation evidence before landing.
